messages.subject: Tiny shade effects
parts:
I'm using the microclimate model with my own data inputs, and am getting only a tiny effect of different shading levels (figure attached). I'm not sure whether this is something that I'm doing wrong in the inputs, or whether it is a real effect. I'm running the model for 12 consecutive days in May, with inputs based on a nearby weather station. I've tried changing the maximum and minimum cloud cover, horizon angles and view factors, but none of these seem to make much difference. Do you have any suggestions for additional inputs that I should check?

Thank you!

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Tiny shade effects
parts:
Hi Rachel,

Which air temperature are you plotting? Is it the reference air temperature, TAREF? If so, you won't see an effect. If it is the local air temperature, TALOC, and you have the reference height Usrhyt set low to the ground, then you should be seeing effects. To be sure if there's something going wrong, try plotting soil surface temperature instead.

Can you post  the relevant code you're using?

Thanks,
Mike

Rachel

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Tiny shade effects
parts:
Hi Rachel

The main issues is that you have probably got the wind speed in the wrong units. It should be m/s - you have max wind speeds of up to 56 m/s which is 200 km/h! Also, try again with a smaller value for the roughness height parameter 'RUF' - you have 30 cm. I tend to use 0.004 for most of the calculations I do and get good matches with observed data. I haven't played around with this parameter very much.

Also, in the next week I'll update the microclimate model to a version that will allow hourly inputs of weather observations. That will require some changes to your code, so be aware of that (there will be an updated vignette from which to base it on).

Hope that helps,
Mike
